selected_result: Stability of fixed precision iterative refinement using a fast multiplication technique

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 12: Iterative Refinement, Problem 12.4

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 12.4: refinement of multiple right-hand sides with the residual computed conventionally and the update computed by a fast method

task_clarification: Suppose GEPP with fixed precision iterative refinement is applied to the multiple right-hand side system A X = B, refining the columns of X in parallel: R = B - A X, A D = R, Y = X + D.
The residual R is computed by conventional multiplication, while the second step uses a fast multiplication technique satisfying only the weaker bound the source labels (13.4).
Formalize the first-order residual conclusion for each refined column y_j: |b_j - A y_j| <= (n + 2) u (|A| |y_j| + |b_j|) + O(u^2), componentwise.

The fast correction computation affects the second-order term through its potentially large fast-multiplication constants; therefore this result alone does not justify claiming an unconditional componentwise backward error of order u.
scope_constraints: The residual is computed conventionally; only the correction solve uses the fast technique.
Use the standard model with unit roundoff u, excluding overflow and underflow.
State the hypotheses required by the one-step fixed-precision refinement analysis, including nonsingularity and the successful GEPP/correction computation.
Represent the refinement step and its rounding assumptions rather than postulating the conclusion.

This frozen benchmark selects the residual bound proved in the Demmel--Higham analysis cited by Problem 12.4 as the precise answer to the book's open-ended question. It must not be replaced by a stronger unconditional stability claim.
